record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: Let E(x_n) be an achievable Cantorval, and let a and b be left endpoints of two distinct interval components of E. Must there exist ε > 0 such that E ∩ [a−ε, a] is a translate of E ∩ [b−ε, b]?

evidence.quote: Is there an analogue of the Nymann–Saenz Lemma for endpoints of interval components of an achievable Cantorval? More precisely, if E(xn) is a Cantorval and a and b are left endpoints of two distinct E-intervals, does there exist ε > 0 such that E ∩ [a − ε, a] is a translate of E ∩ [b − ε, b]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(x_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers with $\sum_{n=1}^\infty x_n < \infty$. Define its achievement set
$$E(x_n) = \Big\{ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n x_n : \varepsilon_n \in \{0,1\} \Big\} \subset \mathbb{R}.$$
A nonempty compact set $C \subset \mathbb{R}$ is called a Cantorval (more precisely, an $\mathcal{M}$-Cantorval) if $C$ is the closure of its interior, every connected component of $C$ that is a nondegenerate closed interval has the property that every neighborhood of it intersects infinitely many other interval components of $C$ as well as infinitely many components that are singletons. Assume $E(x_n)$ is a Cantorval; in this case it is called an achievable Cantorval, and its connected components that are nondegenerate intervals are called $E$-intervals.

Question: Suppose $a$ and $b$ are the left endpoints of two distinct $E$-intervals of an achievable Cantorval $E = E(x_n)$. Must there exist $\varepsilon > 0$ such that
$$E \cap [a-\varepsilon, a] = (E \cap [b-\varepsilon, b]) + (a-b),$$
i.e., $E \cap [a-\varepsilon, a]$ is a translate of $E \cap [b-\varepsilon, b]$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on achievement sets, asking for an analogue of the Nymann–Sáenz lemma at left endpoints of interval components of achievable Cantorvals. No published resolution was found.
